applicableAreas: Western transformer pad
Eastern transformer pad
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) depicts two transformer pads on the site plan drawing. The vision analysis of Sheet 21 confirmed that no dimensions or clearance radii are labeled for either transformer pad. The pads are drawn in proximity to parking areas, driveways, and building footprints, but no specific clearance distances are dimensioned or noted. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows the overall layout with buildings and parking areas but provides no transformer pad clearance dimensions. The preliminary electrical plan shows the general locations of the two transformer pads but provides no evidence of compliance with the minimum clearance requirements specified in UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 (10 ft hot-stick use area, 5 ft sides with operators/controls, 3 ft other sides based on building type and fire rating).
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 requires specific clearances from pad-mounted equipment based on the side of the equipment and building construction type. The required clearances range from 3 feet to 10 feet depending on the side and building characteristics. The applicant's burden is to demonstrate compliance through dimensioned drawings. The absence of any clearance dimensions or notes on the electrical plan and site plan means the requirement cannot be verified. The deficiency is not that compliance might not exist in reality, but that the required documentation is absent. The preliminary design nature of the electrical plan (labeled as 'Preliminary Electrical Design') combined with the complete absence of clearance dimensions indicates this item must be addressed with detailed clearance callouts and notes before the design can be verified as compliant.
findings.comment: Transformer pad clearances from buildings, parking areas, sidewalks, and other structures not shown or dimensioned on electrical design plan. Provide dimensioned clearance details for both transformer pads per UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 (minimum 3 feet to 10 feet depending on side and building type), including verification of building construction type (brick/masonry with 2-hour fire rating vs. non-brick/masonry) for clearance determination.

applicableAreas: Buildings 1 through 8
Overhead electric facilities along western property boundary
Overhead electric facilities along southern property boundary
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows overhead electric facilities (OHE) marked with dashed lines along the western and southern property boundaries. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) also confirms the OHE line running along the southern boundary. Sheets 9 and 31 show the building footprints and layouts throughout the site. However, NO BUILDING ELEVATION SHEETS are included in the site plan submittal to verify the three-dimensional clearance between the proposed buildings and the overhead conductors. The vision analysis of Sheet 21 confirmed that overhead electric facilities are shown along boundaries but no elevation views or clearance exhibits are provided. The buildings shown on the site plan and landscape plan would need elevation drawings to verify they maintain the required 7.5-foot horizontal clearance and 15-foot radial clearance from overhead primary and neutral conductors per UCM § 1.10.3.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 establishes permanent clearance requirements from AE overhead distribution lines (7.5 feet horizontal, 15-foot radius). To verify compliance with these clearance requirements, building elevations must be provided showing the position of overhead conductors, poles, and cross arms relative to the proposed structures. The site plan shows the overhead facilities and building locations in plan view, but without elevation views and clearance exhibits, the three-dimensional clearance relationships cannot be determined. The 'Preliminary' designation of the electrical design may indicate coordination with Austin Energy is ongoing, but the site plan should include the necessary views to verify this critical clearance requirement. Without building elevation sheets showing these facilities, the deficiency status cannot be changed from 'unclear' to 'pass'.
findings.comment: Building elevations not provided showing relationship between proposed structures and overhead electric conductors. Provide building elevation sheets showing electric poles, cross arms (approximately 8 feet wide), and overhead conductors with dimensions confirming minimum 7.5-foot horizontal and 15-foot radial clearances per UCM § 1.10.3.

applicableAreas: Underground electric conduit routing throughout site
Building connections to electrical service
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows underground electric lines (marked as blue solid lines with 'E' markers) routing throughout the site to connect buildings, pull boxes, transformer pads, and meters. The vision analysis confirmed that underground electric conduit is proposed throughout the site. However, there are no dimension lines or notes showing the clearances from the underground electric conduit to customer buildings, foundations, permanent structures, or other utilities. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows building locations but provides no coordination dimensions between buildings and proposed underground electric facilities. The preliminary electrical plan shows the general routing of electric lines but provides no evidence that the minimum 60-inch clearance from buildings per UCM § 1.10.5 has been verified or documented.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5 requires minimum 60-inch (5-foot) horizontal clearance from AE underground cable, conduit, and underground facilities to customer buildings, foundations, or permanent structures. The applicant must document this clearance through dimensioned drawings. The existence of underground electric lines on the preliminary electrical plan does not constitute compliance documentation; the clearances must be explicitly shown and dimensioned. The absence of clearance dimensions or notes demonstrating compliance with the 60-inch minimum clearance requirement means the deficiency cannot be marked as resolved. This is a documentation requirement that must be satisfied through additional detail.
findings.comment: Underground electric cable and conduit clearances from buildings, foundations, and permanent structures not shown or dimensioned on electrical design plan. Provide dimensioned clearance details on utility plan showing minimum 60-inch horizontal clearance from all AE underground facilities to customer buildings, foundations, and permanent structures per UCM § 1.10.5.

applicableAreas: Proposed storm drain and water line crossings with underground electric facilities
findings.observation: Sheet 20 (Utility Tap Public Plan & Profile) shows a profile view of the proposed water line and a plan view indicating the location of proposed underground electric facilities (marked as 'Proposed Underground Electric' with transformer pad symbol). The vision analysis of Sheet 20 confirmed that the plan view shows both water utility and electric utility at the same general location, indicating a crossing or potential conflict. However, the profile view on Sheet 20 only depicts the water line elevations; there is NO cross-section detail showing the vertical relationship, clearance distance, or separation between the water line and the electric conduit at the crossing point. Sheet 12 (Storm Sewer Plan) would show storm drain routing, and if it crosses the proposed underground electric lines shown on Sheet 21, a cross-section detail should be provided. No such detail has been located.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5 requires cross-section details where utilities cross AE underground facilities to demonstrate required clearances. The grouping specifies that when storm drains and water lines cross underground electric lines, cross-section details must be provided showing vertical and horizontal clearance verification. The preliminary electrical plan and utility tap plan show the general locations and routing of utilities, but without cross-section details at crossing locations, the vertical and horizontal clearances cannot be verified. This is a documentation deficiency - the required cross-section views must be provided to demonstrate compliance with utility separation requirements.
findings.comment: Cross-section details not provided where storm drains and water lines cross underground electric conduit and facilities. Provide cross-section details at all utility crossing locations showing minimum 12-inch vertical clearance (24-36 inches for gas/fuel/steam lines) and horizontal separation per UCM § 1.10.5.

applicableAreas: Utility crossings between underground electric lines and water, wastewater, and storm drainage facilities
findings.observation: Sheet 20 (Utility Tap Public Plan & Profile) shows the water utility tap plan and profile but does NOT provide cross-section details showing vertical and horizontal clearances at locations where the water line intersects with the proposed underground electric facilities shown on Sheet 21. Sheet 21 shows underground electric routing throughout the site, and Sheet 20 shows proposed water line routing. These utilities are indicated as crossing or in close proximity in the plan view, but no cross-section engineering drawings are provided demonstrating the specific clearance dimensions at crossing locations. The vision analysis of Sheet 20 confirmed that while utilities are shown in plan view, no cross-section details are provided showing utility separation and clearance.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5 requires that where utilities cross AE underground facilities, cross-section details must be provided that show both vertical and horizontal clearances. These clearances must be dimensioned and verified: minimum 12 inches for water/wastewater, 24-36 inches for gas/fuel/steam, and 12 inches for other utilities. The absence of cross-section views at utility crossing locations is a clear documentation deficiency. The applicant must provide cross-section drawings (not just plan views) showing the three-dimensional relationship of utilities at crossing points to verify clearance compliance. Without these details, the design cannot be verified as compliant.
findings.comment: Cross-section utility design drawings not provided showing vertical and horizontal clearances between underground electric lines and crossing utilities (water, wastewater, storm drainage). Provide cross-section details for each utility crossing showing minimum 12-inch vertical clearance for water/wastewater and minimum clearance distances per UCM § 1.10.5.

applicableAreas: Utility crossing locations throughout the site
findings.observation: Sheet 20 (Utility Tap Public Plan & Profile) includes a profile view of the water line showing vertical elevations (labeled with flowline elevations such as 'FL 8": 674.33'), demonstrating that elevation information is available for water utilities. However, the profile view only depicts the water line and does not show the underground electric facility at crossing locations. No cross-section details with elevation dimensions are provided at locations where utilities cross. The vision analysis confirmed that while the water line profile includes elevation callouts, there are no elevation-detailed cross-sections showing the utility crossing locations or the relative elevations of the electric and water utilities at those points.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5 requires that elevations be provided on utility crossings to demonstrate clearance compliance. The grouping specifies 'Elevations not provided on utility crossings' as a deficiency. While Sheet 20 provides a profile with elevations for the water line, it does not provide cross-sectional details with elevations at the actual crossing point with the electric utility. The absence of elevation dimensions at utility crossing locations prevents verification of the vertical clearance requirement. Cross-section details with labeled elevations for both utilities at crossing points must be provided.
findings.comment: Elevations not provided on utility crossing details where electric facilities cross storm drains and water lines. Provide cross-section details with vertical elevation dimensions showing how utilities cross and the separation distance maintained between them.

applicableAreas: All proposed buildings
Relationship to existing Valley View Road, poles, and streetlights
findings.observation: The site plan submittal (39 sheets total) contains detailed site plans, grading plans, utility plans, and landscape plans, but does NOT include any building elevation sheets. Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) shows existing site features and property context, but no building elevation views have been identified in the submittal. UCM § 1.16.0(2) requires building elevations showing the relationship between proposed structures and existing public infrastructure including streets, streetlights, and electric poles. The absence of building elevation sheets representing the buildings' relationship to Valley View Road and any adjacent utility poles/streetlights is a clear deficiency in the required documentation.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(2) explicitly requires building elevations to show the relationship between proposed structures and existing streets, streetlights, and electric poles. These elevation views are essential for demonstrating clearance compliance and understanding site context. The site plan submittal includes plan views and details but lacks the elevation views specifically required by code. This is a documentation requirement that must be satisfied through the addition of building elevation sheets for all buildings, showing their relationship to Valley View Road and any adjacent utility infrastructure.
findings.comment: Building elevations not provided showing proposed structures with adjacent streets (Valley View Road), streetlights, and electric poles. Provide front and side elevations for all buildings showing the relationship to Valley View Road, existing poles, and overhead/underground facilities per UCM § 1.16.0(2).

applicableAreas: Relationship between Buildings 1-8 and electric easements on property
findings.observation: The site plan documents show electric easements on the grading plan (Sheet 11) labeled as '5' Electric Easement' and '15' Electric Easement' located along property boundaries. However, there are no building elevation sheets showing the three-dimensional relationship between the proposed buildings and these electric easements. The code requires building elevations to show this relationship. Sheet 9 shows buildings and easement boundaries in plan view, but plan view alone does not adequately demonstrate the spatial relationship required by code. The absence of building elevation sheets means the required relationship documentation is missing.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(2) requires building elevations to show the relationship between proposed buildings and electric easements/facilities. This is distinct from plan view representation. Elevations provide a view perpendicular to the lot line and show how buildings sit relative to easement areas, heights above easement grades, and clearances. Without elevation views, this required documentation cannot be verified. Building elevation sheets must be provided to show all buildings' relationships to the electric easements depicted on the property.
findings.comment: Building elevations not provided showing relationship between proposed buildings and electric easements on property. Provide building elevation views from the direction of electric easements showing the spatial relationship between structures and easement areas per UCM § 1.16.0(2).

applicableAreas: Overhead electric facilities shown on boundaries
Proposed buildings relative to OHE facilities
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows overhead electric facilities (OHE) marked with dashed lines labeled '- OHE -' along the western and southern property boundaries. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) also confirms the OHE line along the southern boundary. However, NO BUILDING ELEVATION SHEETS are included in the site plan submittal. Elevation sheets are required to show electric poles, overhead lines, conductors, cross arms, and property boundaries in relation to the proposed buildings. The plan views show the overhead facilities and buildings but cannot adequately depict the pole positions, conductor heights, cross arm widths, or vertical clearances to buildings.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(2) explicitly requires building elevation sheets to show 'electric poles, overhead lines, conductors, cross arms, and property boundaries.' Plan view representation is insufficient. Building elevations provide the engineer and reviewer with the necessary three-dimensional perspective to understand conductor positions, pole heights, cross arm configurations (approximately 8 feet wide per the grouping regulatory overview), and vertical clearances to building surfaces. Without elevation sheets, the required documentation is missing and clearance compliance cannot be verified.
findings.comment: Electric poles, overhead lines, conductors, cross arms, and property boundaries not shown on building elevation sheets. Provide building elevations showing all overhead electric facilities with conductors, poles (with dimensions for cross arms approximately 8 feet wide), and property boundaries per UCM § 1.16.0(2).

applicableAreas: Retaining walls along property boundaries near electric easements
findings.observation: Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) shows retaining walls labeled along property boundaries: 'Begin Concrete Retaining Wall', 'Tie into existing Retaining Wall Match existing Wall Elevations', 'Existing Retaining Wall', and 'Existing Retaining Wall to be Replaced'. The grading plan also shows electric easements ('5' Electric Easement', '15' Electric Easement') in the same boundary areas where retaining walls are located. However, the retaining wall heights (top and bottom elevations) are not clearly labeled on the grading plan in the areas near the electric easements. Sheets 38-39 (Wall Plan Details and Notes) would contain the detailed wall cross-sections and footing details. These details must be reviewed to determine if wall elevations and footing details near overhead electric facilities are adequately documented.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires that retaining wall heights and footing details be shown on grading plans when walls are proposed near overhead electric facilities to verify that the wall construction does not create clearance violations. The grouping specifies that 'Retaining wall heights (top and bottom elevations) not shown on grading plans or toe and heel footing details not provided for retaining walls near overhead electric facilities' is a deficiency. While walls are shown on Sheet 11 near electric easements, the specific top and bottom elevations are not clearly called out in those boundary areas. Whether detailed wall sections on Sheets 38-39 adequately document these clearances requires visual examination. The unclear status reflects uncertainty about whether the detail sheets (38-39) contain the required information.
findings.comment: Retaining wall heights and footing details near electric easements not clearly documented on grading plan. Provide wall top and bottom elevations on grading plan for walls located near overhead electric easements, with detailed cross-sections showing toe and heel footing configuration to verify clearance compliance per UCM § 1.10.3.

applicableAreas: Proposed buildings 1-8 relative to existing overhead electric facilities
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows overhead electric facilities (OHE) along the western and southern property boundaries. Sheets 9, 21, and 31 show the locations of the proposed buildings relative to these overhead facilities in plan view. However, NO PLAN AND PROFILE VIEWS have been provided that show the vertical (profile) relationship between the existing overhead electric lines and the proposed buildings. UCM § 1.16.0(2) requires 'Plan and profile not submitted to verify required clearances between existing electric lines and proposed buildings.' The site plan includes plan views showing the buildings and OHE lines, but the profile views (cross-section views showing elevation differences) required to verify clearances are not present in the submittal.
findings.reasoning: Plan view alone is insufficient to verify clearance compliance between overhead conductors and building structures. Profile views (also called cross-sections in plan direction) are required to show the vertical separation between conductor height and building height/roofline. Without these profile views with dimensions, the clearance requirement of 7.5 feet horizontal and 15-foot radial separation cannot be verified. The code specifically requires 'plan and profile' views be submitted. The current submittal contains only plan views for this relationship.
findings.comment: Plan and profile views not submitted to verify required clearances between existing overhead electric lines and proposed buildings. Provide plan and profile cross-sections showing vertical separation between overhead conductors and building structures, with dimensions confirming 7.5-foot horizontal and 15-foot radial clearances per UCM § 1.10.3 and UCM § 1.16.0(2).

applicableAreas: Coversheet, grading plan, landscape plan
findings.observation: Sheet 3 (General Notes / Coversheet) contains detailed Electric Transmission Notes in Block 20, including 16 specific notes about transmission line clearances, safety meetings, barricading, access, and structural load requirements. These notes appear on the coversheet. The utility plan (Sheet 21) shows OHE (overhead electric) facilities marked as dashed lines along property boundaries. However, the vision analysis of the electrical plan and visual examination of other sheets indicate that the OHE shown on the property boundaries appear to be DISTRIBUTION facilities (poles and conductors along the boundary), NOT TRANSMISSION facilities (large steel transmission structures with 60kV+ voltage). The site plan does not depict any transmission line easement boundaries, transmission structures, or transmission-specific infrastructure. The checklist item requires determining: (1) whether transmission facilities exist, and if they do, transmission notes must be present on coversheet, grading plan, and landscape plan; or (2) if transmission does NOT exist, transmission notes should be removed. The extensive transmission notes currently on the coversheet suggest transmission facilities were expected but may not actually exist, or the engineer included them as a standard template.
findings.reasoning: The grouping distinguishes between 'transmission' (60kV+ voltage, large structures, transmission easements) and 'distribution' (less than 60kV, typical pole-mounted infrastructure). The presence of transmission notes on the coversheet suggests the design team anticipated transmission facilities on or near the site. However, visual review of the electrical plan and other documents shows only distribution facilities (OHE poles and conductors). The facts.md file did not identify any transmission easement or transmission structure on the property. This creates ambiguity: either (a) transmission facilities exist and are not properly depicted on plans, or (b) transmission notes were included as template language and should be removed. Without clear identification of whether transmission facilities are present, the status cannot be definitively 'pass' or 'fail'. The condition is UNCLEAR and requires clarification from the applicant regarding whether transmission infrastructure is present on or adjacent to the site.
findings.comment: Transmission notes appear on coversheet (Sheet 3) but no transmission structures or transmission easements are evident on electrical plan or utility plan. Clarify whether transmission facilities (60kV+ voltage level) are present on or adjacent to the site. If no transmission facilities exist, remove transmission notes from coversheet, grading plan, and landscape plan per UCM § 1.16.0(8). If transmission facilities do exist, ensure all required transmission notes appear on all applicable sheets.

applicableAreas: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21)
findings.observation: Sheet 21 is titled 'Preliminary Electrical Design Plan' which by definition suggests the electrical design is conceptual and not final. However, no explicit disclaimer note is visible on the sheet stating that 'electric facilities shown are conceptual and not for final design' or similar language. The coversheet (Sheet 3) and utility plan notes do not contain a visible note stating that the electric design is preliminary and not to be used for construction. The presence of the word 'Preliminary' in the sheet title provides some indication of design phase, but the checklist item requires an explicit note on the plans stating the facilities are conceptual and not final. The vision analysis of Sheet 21 did not identify such a disclaimer note in the visible text blocks.
findings.reasoning: The grouping specifies that when electric facilities are shown conceptually (i.e., when Austin Energy Design has not completed final design), plans must include disclaimers that facilities are conceptual and not for bidding purposes. The sheet title 'Preliminary Electrical Design Plan' suggests preliminary status, but this title alone may not be sufficient to serve as the required notice to contractors and builders. An explicit note stating something like 'The electric facilities shown on this plan are preliminary and conceptual. Do not use for bidding purposes. Final electrical design will be coordinated with Austin Energy' should be clearly visible as a text note on the electrical plan or coversheet. The absence of such an explicit disclaimer note, despite the preliminary design status, creates an unclear situation.
findings.comment: Plans do not clearly note that electric facilities shown are conceptual and not final design. Add explicit note to utility plan and/or coversheet stating: 'The electric facilities shown on this plan are preliminary and conceptual. Final electrical design will be coordinated with and approved by Austin Energy. These plans are not for bidding or construction purposes.'

applicableAreas: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan
findings.observation: Sheet 21 is titled 'Preliminary Electrical Design Plan,' indicating the electrical design is conceptual. However, the vision analysis of Sheet 21 and the utility notes block reviewed did not identify an explicit note stating 'The electric facility layout shown should not be used for bidding purposes' or equivalent language. The grouping states that when electric facilities are shown conceptually (not final AE Design), plans should include a note about not using the design for bidding. While the preliminary status is indicated in the sheet title, an explicit disclaimer note appears to be absent.
findings.reasoning: When electrical designs are preliminary and not finalized by Austin Energy, contractor and bidders must be explicitly warned not to use the preliminary design for estimating or construction. The sheet title 'Preliminary' provides some indication but may not be sufficient notice. A clear, prominent note stating the plans should not be used for bidding purposes is the more reliable method to communicate this requirement. The absence of such an explicit note constitutes a documentation deficiency, even if the preliminary status is indicated in the sheet title.
findings.comment: Plans do not include note that electric facility layout shown should not be used for bidding purposes. Add explicit note to electrical plan and/or coversheet: 'This is a preliminary electrical design plan. These plans should not be used for bidding, material takeoff, or construction purposes. Final design will be provided by Austin Energy.'

applicableAreas: Plat or coversheet
findings.observation: Sheet 2 (Plat) was examined and found to contain only historical plat notes from the original 1975 Mecey Subdivision dedication and does not include any notes regarding Austin Energy rights. The vision analysis of Sheet 2 confirmed: 'There are NO notes anywhere on this sheet regarding any of the specified Austin Energy (AE) requirements... there is no mention of: AE rights to prune trees and maintain easements.' Sheet 3 (Coversheet/General Notes) does contain an electric note (Block 8) that states: 'Austin Energy has the right to prune and/or remove trees, shrubbery and other obstructions to the extent necessary to keep the easements clear.' However, this note appears on the coversheet (Sheet 3), not on the plat sheet (Sheet 2). UCM § 1.16.0(8)(i) requires that this plat note appear on the plat itself or be incorporated by reference.
findings.reasoning: The code requirement is for a 'plat note' - which traditionally means a note that appears on the recorded plat document. While Sheet 3 (coversheet) contains the required language about Austin Energy pruning rights, the plat sheet (Sheet 2) itself does not contain this note. Having the note on the coversheet may provide general project notice, but it does not satisfy the specific requirement for a 'plat note.' To ensure the pruning right restriction is recorded with the property and binds future owners, the note should appear directly on the plat sheet. The current documentation does not meet the literal requirement for a plat note.
findings.comment: Plat note regarding Austin Energy right to prune and remove trees and obstructions not shown on plat sheet. Add plat note: 'Austin Energy has the right to prune and to remove trees, shrubbery and other obstructions to the extent necessary to keep all electric facility easements clear' per UCM § 1.16.0(8)(i).

applicableAreas: Plat or coversheet
findings.observation: Sheet 2 (Plat) does not contain any note regarding owner responsibility for tree pruning or removal within 10 feet of overhead facilities. The vision analysis confirmed no such notes exist on the plat. Sheet 3 (Coversheet) contains electric notes (Block 8) that reference tree pruning responsibility: 'The owner shall be responsible for installation of temporary erosion control, revegetation and tree protection. In addition, the owner shall be responsible for any initial tree pruning and tree removal that is within ten feet of the center line of the proposed overhead electric facilities...' However, this appears on the coversheet, not as a plat note on Sheet 2.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(8)(iii) requires a plat note specifying owner responsibility for initial tree pruning and removal within 10 feet of the centerline of proposed overhead electric facilities. While similar language appears on the coversheet (Sheet 3), the specific requirement is for a plat note - which means the note should appear on the plat document itself to bind the property and provide notice to future owners. The plat sheet (Sheet 2) does not contain this note, representing a deficiency in the required plat documentation.
findings.comment: Plat note regarding owner responsibility for tree pruning within 10 feet of proposed overhead facilities not shown on plat. Add plat note: 'Owner shall be responsible for initial tree pruning and tree removal that is within ten feet of the centerline of the proposed overhead electric facilities' per UCM § 1.16.0(8)(iii).

applicableAreas: Plat or coversheet
findings.observation: Sheet 2 (Plat) was examined and contains no note regarding temporary erosion control, revegetation, or tree protection responsibility. The vision analysis confirmed: 'There are NO notes...regarding...Temporary erosion control and tree protection responsibility.' Sheet 3 (Coversheet/General Notes, Block 8) does contain relevant language: 'The owner shall be responsible for installation of temporary erosion control, revegetation and tree protection.' However, this language appears on the coversheet (Sheet 3), not on the plat document (Sheet 2) itself.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(8)(iii) requires that a plat note be added specifying owner responsibility for temporary erosion control, revegetation, and tree protection. While Sheet 3 (coversheet) contains general project notes with similar language, the specific code requirement is for a 'plat note' - meaning a note that should appear on the recorded plat to bind the property with this obligation. The absence of this note on Sheet 2 (Plat) constitutes a deficiency in the required plat documentation, even if similar language appears elsewhere in the project notes.
findings.comment: Plat note regarding owner responsibility for temporary erosion control, revegetation, and tree protection not shown on plat. Add plat note: 'Owner shall be responsible for installation of temporary erosion control, revegetation and tree protection during construction' per UCM § 1.16.0(8)(iii).

applicableAreas: Plat or coversheet
findings.observation: Sheet 2 (Plat) does not contain a note regarding owner responsibility to maintain NESC, NEC, OSHA, City, and Texas clearances. The vision analysis confirmed the absence of such notes on the plat. Sheet 3 (Coversheet, Block 8) contains related language: 'The owner of the property is responsible for maintaining clearances required by the National Electric Safety Code, Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) regulations, City of Austin rules and regulations and Texas state laws...' However, this appears on the coversheet, not as a plat note on Sheet 2.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(8)(iv) requires a plat note establishing that the owner is responsible for maintaining clearances per NESC, NEC, OSHA, City, and Texas requirements. This note should appear on the plat document itself to clearly bind the property and provide enduring notice to the owner and successors. While language addressing this requirement exists on Sheet 3 (coversheet), the plat document (Sheet 2) lacks this specific required note. A plat note is the appropriate vehicle for establishing a property-level obligation that runs with the land.
findings.comment: Plat note regarding owner responsibility to maintain NESC, NEC, OSHA, City, and Texas clearances not shown on plat. Add plat note: 'Owner is responsible for maintaining clearances required by the National Electric Safety Code, Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) regulations, City of Austin rules and regulations, and Texas state laws' per UCM § 1.16.0(8)(iv).
